evidence: For a fair evaluation, five cross-validation splits are conducted and the mean is measured.
An ensemble ML classifier, known as Extra Trees, that belongs to the trees family has been utilised for this purpose.
Various classification metrics are collected such as accuracy, Area Under the Curve (AUC), F1 Score, Detection Rate (DR), False Alarm Rate (FAR) and time required to predict a single test sample
The datasets have been split into 70%-30% for training and testing purposes.
unresolved: n_datasets=4 counts the distinct source NIDS datasets (UNSW-NB15, BoT-IoT, ToN-IoT, CSE-CIC-IDS2018); the paper also derives a 5th merged dataset (NF-UQ-NIDS) and evaluates 3 feature-set variants (original, basic NetFlow-v1, proposed NetFlow-v2) per source, yielding up to 14 dataset-variant rows in Table 8 -- not counted separately here since they are feature-set variants, not independent corpora.

n_seeds=5 is inferred from 'five cross-validation splits ... the mean is measured' -- this is 5-fold CV repetition, not independently seeded reruns in the random-seed sense; only the mean is reported, no per-fold values or std/CI.
n_baselines=2 counts the original proprietary feature set and the basic 12-feature NetFlow (v1) set as comparison baselines against the proposed 43-feature NetFlow-v2 set.
control_arm is not applicable to this paper (no backdoor/poisoning context); set to 'none' as the closest schema fit.
